_notes: Shared SolNet vocabulary, hand-extracted from RFC-2300 (Terminology & Concepts), sections 1-7 only. Not itself a protocol/hardware content file -- this is the canonical vocabulary/constants other db/ content files should reference by name rather than reinventing (RFC-2300: 'Lock this first; all RFCs must reference these definitions'). Deliberately excludes RFC-2300 sections 8-15 (TLV Key Registry, Error Handling, Security Considerations, Interoperability, Operational Behavior, Conformance, Document Maintenance, Registry Procedures) -- that content reads like RFC-2350 (Canonical Addressing)'s actual subject, not terminology; flagged in db/CORPUS-STATUS.md rather than corrected, since RFC files get surgical corrections only. Converted from YAML to JSON 2026-09-04 per project format decision (see db/README.md).

UUID_S7.description: 128-bit, time-sortable identifier, UUIDv7-compatible, extended for ledger friendliness. Canonical NetworkID for ledger-anchored identity and cross-domain references. MUST be used at the point identity is anchored, audited, or enforced across domains; local systems MAY use other schemes internally until that point.

address_grammar.rule: exactly one // boundary; parsers MUST enforce it

LocationChain.meaning: identity authority, trust domain, coarse location

ServiceChain.meaning: internal domain structure, service path (locally resolved)

role_weight.meaning: how strongly a node participates in each plane
role_weight.mismatch_behavior: when advertised role weight conflicts with observed behavior, systems log AuditEvents and increase verification steps

device_identity_hierarchy._notes: answers a different question at each layer, per RFC-2300 section 6.1 -- the RFC-2301 key hierarchy (db/trust/rfc2301-key-hierarchy.json) is the concrete cryptographic instantiation of this same layering

layers.answers: is the device what it claims to be
is the device still under expected control
is this specific interaction current and authorized
who/what is the device acting for (no global anchoring required)
who authorized this action, if the actor isn't the ultimate authority

canonical_record_types._notes: RFC-2300 section 8 (the terminology-appropriate list) -- confirms the record names already used elsewhere in db/ are real canonical names, not invented ones
canonical_record_types.common_requirement: all records MUST include provenance and freshness metadata

confidence_model.rule: when freshness is uncertain, consumers treat records as advisory and increase verification steps. Delayed ledger writes force UNVERIFIED mode with reduced privileges (RFC-2300 section 4.2, section 9.1 stress behavior).
